rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is empty, so the first experiment should test a promising multimodal configuration. This experiment tests combining RNA (scvi_n200) and image (imagenet_vit_l) data with weighted fusion, which is a common and effective approach. It clarifies whether multimodal integration can outperform single-modality baselines, and it uses established encoders to reduce uncertainty about key design choices.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal configurations with weighted fusion (config_002) achieve 0.537 validation accuracy. This experiment tests multiprofile settings with transformer aggregation and concat fusion, which are critical design choices with potential to improve performance. It balances exploration by testing a new profile setting and aggregation method while building on the previous multimodal approach.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal multiprofile setups with pca_n2000 RNA and transformer aggregation (config_004, 0.598 accuracy) are promising. This experiment tests resnet50 image encoder and weighted fusion (vs. config_004's concat fusion) to clarify whether fusion method improvements can further boost performance. It balances exploration of critical design choices (fusion strategy) while building on the successful transformer aggregation approach.

The existing evidence shows config_004 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000 RNA, imagenet_vit_l image, transformer aggregation, concat fusion) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.598). This experiment tests changing the fusion method from concat to weighted while keeping other parameters identical, which could clarify if fusion strategy significantly impacts performance. It balances exploitation (building on the best config) and exploration (testing a critical design choice).

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile settings and transformer aggregation perform best (config_004: 0.5988 accuracy). This experiment tests using scgpt (a more advanced RNA encoder) with resnet50 image encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion, which could improve performance by leveraging better RNA encoding while maintaining the effective image and aggregation settings from the current top performer.

Existing evidence shows config_004 (pca_n2000 RNA, imagenet_vit_l image, transformer aggregation, concat fusion) has the highest accuracy (0.5988). This experiment tests whether switching to resnet50 image encoder (config_007) with the same aggregation/fusion settings improves performance, clarifying the impact of image encoder choice. This balances exploitation of current top-performing parameters with exploration of a key design choice (image encoder).

Existing evidence shows that multimodal multiprofile models with pca_n2000 RNA and imagenet_vit_l image encoders achieve the highest accuracy (0.5988). This experiment tests avgpool aggregation (vs. transformer in config_004) with concat fusion, clarifying whether simpler aggregation improves performance. It balances exploration of aggregation methods while maintaining proven components.

The existing evidence shows config_049 (avgpool aggregation, concat fusion) achieves the highest validation accuracy (0.6287). This experiment tests changing the fusion method to weighted while keeping RNA/image encoders and aggregation the same, to determine if fusion strategy impacts performance. It clarifies whether weighted fusion could improve upon the current best, balancing exploitation of the top-performing setup with exploration of key design choices.

The existing evidence shows config_013 (avgpool+weighted) achieves the highest accuracy (0.635). This experiment tests scvi_n200 RNA encoder with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion, which could potentially improve performance by combining the strengths of transformer aggregation (config_005, 0.585) with the top fusion method. It addresses uncertainty about RNA encoder choice (scvi_n200 vs pca_n2000) and aggregation method, offering a logical extension to the top-performing config_013.

The existing evidence shows config_045 (0.725 accuracy) is the top performer with scvi_n200 RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion. This experiment tests the same RNA and image encoders but with avgpool aggregation instead of transformer. This clarifies whether aggregation method impacts performance, balancing exploitation of current best and exploration of critical design choices. Since the budget is exhausted, testing this closely related configuration provides final insight into key hyperparameters.
